title_en: 279: How AI and Interest Rates Are Changing Corporate Credit Markets
title_zh: AI 与利率如何改变公司信用市场｜BlackRock 的 Jose Aguilar、Tony Kim 与 Jean Boivin
subtitle_zh: AI 巨额资本开支推高借贷成本，信用投资者要学会辨认颠覆中的输家。
summary_zh: 本期 The Bid 由 BlackRock 主持人 Oscar Pulido 主讲，穿插三位嘉宾观点：欧洲信用业务主管 Jose Aguilar、基本面股票团队全球科技组负责人 Tony Kim、全球投资与组合解决方案主管 Jean Boivin。节目从公司信用市场（corporate credit markets）切入，核心论点是：AI 的故事不只是找出下一个大赢家，更要识别哪些企业会被抛下。第一，资本争夺推高融资成本——Tony Kim 说 AI 时代等于重建一张全新的互联网，数据中心在算力、能耗、规模上都要高一个数量级；五年 7 万亿美元的资本开支（CAPEX）造成对资本的激烈竞争，连与 AI 关系不大的借款人也要付更高利息。第二，风险常在资本结构而非行业——Jose Aguilar 回顾 2022 年利率急升后的经验，指出出问题的往往不是商业模式或行业，而是资本结构，多数靠股东注资加债权人展期化解；若利率持续偏高，部分企业还得重回谈判桌。第三，AI 带来经营性颠覆——软件技术栈最上层的应用与服务已出现 SaaS 末日式担忧，数万亿美元价值从应用层流向模型与算力层；拥有专有数据、渠道与不可或缺性的大型软件公司正被市场区分出来，而区域性强、防御性弱、在高估值期被高杠杆收购的小型软件公司压力更大，不过 Jose 强调这并不意味着软件业会出现大规模违约潮。Jean Boivin 则提醒：输家会比赢家更早清晰。本集的价值在于把 AI 叙事从选股视角切换到信用视角——债券投资者关心的不是增长上限，而是偿付能力。
description: 279: How AI and Interest Rates Are Changing Corporate Credit Markets

turns.en: Artificial Intelligence has been one of the biggest investment stories of the past several years. And behind the billions of dollars being invested are companies making decisions about how to finance their businesses. Some are borrowing to expand while others are figuring out whether their existing businesses
turns.zh: 人工智能（Artificial Intelligence）是过去几年最重大的投资故事之一。而在这数百亿美元投资的背后，是一家家公司在为如何给自己的业务融资做决策。有些公司在借钱扩张，另一些则在琢磨自己现有的业务

turns.en: can survive the disruption that AI might bring. So what happens when the same technology creating enormous opportunities for some companies begins to threaten others? And how can investors understand which businesses might be able to repay their debts and which could find themselves in trouble?
turns.zh: 能不能熬过 AI 可能带来的颠覆（disruption）。那么，当同一项技术给一些公司创造了巨大机会、却开始威胁到另一些公司时，会发生什么？投资者又该如何判断哪些企业有能力偿还债务、哪些可能陷入困境？

turns.en: Welcome to the bit where we break down what's happening in the markets and explore the forces changing the economy and finance. I'm Oscar Polito. Today we're looking at the corporate credit markets where companies borrow money and investors lend it to them. And we're going to explore how artificial intelligence, higher interest rates, and
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 The Bid，在这里我们拆解市场上正在发生的事，探讨那些正在改变经济和金融的力量。我是 Oscar Pulido。今天我们聊的是公司信用市场（corporate credit markets）——公司在这里借钱，投资者在这里把钱借给它们。我们要探讨的是，人工智能、更高的利率，以及

turns.en: changing business models are creating new questions about risk. We'll hear from Jose Aguilar, BlackRock's head of European credit, along with insights from some of our conversations throughout the year. To understand why the AI story isn't just about identifying the next big winner, it's also
turns.zh: 不断变化的商业模式，正在带来关于风险的新问题。我们会听到 BlackRock 欧洲信用业务主管 Jose Aguilar 的观点，还有我们今年一系列对话中的洞见。要理解为什么 AI 的故事不只是找出下一个大赢家，它同样

turns.en: about recognizing which businesses could be left behind. To understand why this matters for credit markets, we first need to look at the extraordinary amount of money being invested in AI. When we think about artificial intelligence, we might picture a chatbot answering questions or software helping us work more efficiently.
turns.zh: 关乎识别出哪些企业可能会被抛下。要理解这一点为什么对信用市场很重要，我们首先得看看投入 AI 的资金规模有多惊人。提到人工智能，我们脑海里浮现的可能是一个回答问题的聊天机器人，或者是帮我们更高效工作的软件。

turns.en: But making that technology possible requires something much more physical, enormous data centers, advanced semiconductors, electricity, and the infrastructure to connect it all. When I joined Tony Kim, head of the global technology team within BlackRock fundamental
turns.zh: 但让这项技术成为现实，需要的是一些实在得多的东西：规模庞大的数据中心（data centers）、先进的半导体（semiconductors）、电力，以及把这一切连接起来的基础设施。当我跟着 BlackRock 基本面

turns.en: equities on his annual technology tour in Silicon Valley, he described just how different that infrastructure is becoming. We need to build an entirely new internet. The internet pre-AI was built on a very basic foundation of chips, very little power, small data centers, CPUs, a little bit of memory.
turns.zh: 股票团队全球科技组负责人 Tony Kim 一起参加他在 Silicon Valley 的年度科技巡访时，他描述了这套基础设施正在变得多么不同。我们需要建一张全新的互联网。AI 之前的那张互联网，建立在非常基础的芯片之上：用电很少、数据中心很小，就是 CPU 加一点点内存。

turns.en: Today's data centers and tomorrow's data centers are an order of magnitude more compute, order of magnitude more energy, order of magnitude bigger. That build out is creating opportunities across the economy. But it also raises an important question. Where does the money to finance all this investment come from?
turns.zh: 今天的数据中心和未来的数据中心，算力要高一个数量级（order of magnitude）、能耗要高一个数量级、规模要大一个数量级。这场建设浪潮正在给整个经济创造机会。但它也提出了一个重要问题：为这一切投资融资的钱，从哪里来？

turns.en: Some of the world's largest technology companies can fund significant portions of their spending from the cash their businesses generate. Others may need to borrow money. And as the demand for capital grows, the cost of borrowing becomes an increasingly important part of the story.
turns.zh: 世界上一些最大的科技公司，可以用自己业务产生的现金来支付相当大一部分开支。另一些公司则可能需要借钱。而随着资本需求的增长，借贷成本就成了这个故事里越来越重要的一环。

turns.en: BlackRock's global head of investment and portfolio solutions explained how the scale of AI investment could affect borrowing costs across the broader economy. So 7 trillion over five years of CAPEX to build the infrastructure. That is creating intense competition for capital.
turns.zh: BlackRock 全球投资与组合解决方案主管解释了 AI 投资的规模会如何影响整个经济的借贷成本。所以，五年里 7 万亿美元的资本开支（CAPEX）用来建基础设施，这就造成了对资本的激烈竞争。

turns.en: And so every borrower, governments, companies, all having to pay more for their slice of the available pool of capital. So even companies that have little direct involvement in AI could find themselves paying more to borrow money. And that brings us to corporate credit where understanding a company's ability to manage
turns.zh: 于是每一个借款人——政府、公司——都要为自己在那一池可用资本里分到的份额付出更高的代价。所以，哪怕是和 AI 几乎没什么直接关系的公司，也可能发现自己借钱变贵了。这就把我们带到了公司信用这个领域，在这里，理解一家公司管理

turns.en: his debt becomes particularly important. Let's talk about corporate credit. When it's simplest, when a company issues a bond, it's borrowing money from investors. In exchange, the company typically agrees to make regular interest payments and repay the amount borrowed when the bond matures.
turns.zh: 自身债务的能力就变得特别重要。我们来聊聊公司信用。最简单的情况是：一家公司发行债券（bond），就是在向投资者借钱。作为交换，公司通常承诺定期支付利息，并在债券到期时偿还借入的本金。

turns.en: For investors, corporate bonds can provide a source of income. For companies, they're a way to raise money. To invest, expand their operations, or refinance existing debt. But there's a fundamental difference between lending money to a company and buying its stock.
turns.zh: 对投资者来说，公司债券（corporate bonds）可以提供一份收入来源。对公司来说，债券是一种融资方式，用来投资、扩张业务，或者对现有债务再融资（refinance）。但把钱借给一家公司，和买入它的股票，两者之间有一个根本的区别。

turns.en: As a shareholder, you're hoping the value of the business will grow over time. As a bondholder, you're primarily concerned with whether the company can meet its obligations and repay what it owes. And that means understanding not just how a company is performing today, but what could go wrong in the future.
turns.zh: 作为股东（shareholder），你指望的是这家企业的价值随时间增长。作为债券持有人（bondholder），你最关心的是公司能不能履约、能不能还清欠款。这意味着你不仅要了解一家公司今天经营得怎么样，还要判断未来可能出什么问题。

turns.en: I recently sat down with Jose Aguilar, BlackRock's head of European credit, to discuss how investors assess those risks. That's why it's important to have a process, to have a team, to have access to information and to the companies to really understand that risk. And underwrite the actual bear cases scenario, right?
turns.zh: 我最近和 BlackRock 欧洲信用业务主管 Jose Aguilar 坐下来聊了聊，讨论投资者该如何评估这些风险。这就是为什么有一套流程、有一支团队、能拿到信息、能接触到公司本身，从而真正理解那种风险，是非常重要的。而且还要对真正的熊市情景（bear case）去做承保评估（underwrite），对吧？

turns.en: What we try to do is always think about what can go wrong in credit and think the real risk that that company will have in terms of paying us that coupon and that principle at the end of the period. In other words, it's not enough to look at the interest rate a company is offering investors.
turns.zh: 我们一直在做的，就是始终去想信用上可能出什么问题，去想那家公司在期末付给我们票息（coupon）和本金（principal）这件事上，真正的风险有多大。换句话说，光看一家公司给投资者的利率是不够的。

turns.en: You also need to understand the business behind that bond. Consider two hypothetical companies that borrowed money a few years ago when interest rates were close to zero. One has a strong balance sheet, reliable revenues, and relatively little debt.
turns.zh: 你还得理解那只债券背后的生意。设想两家假想的公司，它们在几年前利率接近零的时候借了钱。一家有强健的资产负债表（balance sheet）、可靠的收入和相对较少的债务。

turns.en: The other has borrowed heavily and depends on continued growth to meet its financial obligations. Now imagine both companies need to refinance their borrowing at today's higher interest rates. For the first company, the additional cost might be manageable, but for the second, those
turns.zh: 另一家则大举借债，靠持续增长来履行自己的财务义务。现在想象这两家公司都需要在今天更高的利率水平下对借款再融资。对第一家公司来说，多出来的成本也许还扛得住；但对第二家来说，那些

turns.en: higher interest payments could put significant pressure on its finances. And that's important because a company doesn't necessarily have to be losing money or operating in a declining industry to encounter financial difficulties. Sometimes the problem is simply that the debt it took on has become too expensive.
turns.zh: 更高的利息支出可能会给它的财务带来巨大压力。这一点很重要，因为一家公司并不一定非得是在亏钱、或者处在一个衰退的行业里，才会遇到财务困难。有时候问题很简单：它当初背上的债务变得太贵了。

turns.en: Jose explained that this was something credit markets had already experienced following the sharp rise in interest rates in 2022. It wasn't a problem with the best model of the company, it wasn't a problem with the sector, it was a problem with the capital structure, and in most of the situations sponsors
turns.zh: Jose 解释说，在 2022 年利率急剧上升之后，信用市场其实已经经历过这种情况了。问题不在于公司的商业模式，也不在于所处的行业，问题在于资本结构（capital structure）。而且在大多数情况下，股权发起方（sponsors）

turns.en: or equity holders contributed to adding a little bit of equity and bond holders or loan holders, they agreed to extend the maturity. What Jose is describing is a situation where lenders and business owners work together to give a company more time to repay its debts, sometimes with shareholders contributing additional money.
turns.zh: 或者股东会出资注入一点股本，而债券持有人或贷款持有人则同意展期（extend the maturity）。Jose 描述的正是这样一种情形：债权人和企业主一起合作，给公司更多时间去偿还债务，有时股东还会额外注资。

turns.en: The distinction is important, a company can have a viable business but still face financial pressure because of the way it is financed itself. And while some businesses have been able to manage those pressures, others could find themselves facing difficult decisions if interest rates remain elevated.
turns.zh: 这个区分很重要：一家公司可以有一门站得住脚的生意，却因为自己的融资方式而面临财务压力。虽然有些企业已经能够应对这些压力，但如果利率一直维持在高位，另一些企业可能就会发现自己面临艰难的选择。

turns.en: We have gone through that already, clearly some of those and men and extents and some of those capital structures were still hoping for a lower interest rate environment. So if we see a higher or consistently higher level of interest rates, we may see some of those will have to go back to the negotiation table.
turns.zh: 我们已经经历过一轮了，显然那些修改与展期（amendments and extensions）安排当中，有一些资本结构仍然在盼着一个更低的利率环境。所以，如果我们看到利率处在更高的、或者持续更高的水平，可能会看到其中一些不得不重新回到谈判桌前。

turns.en: But higher borrowing costs are only part of the equation because the other question investors have to consider is whether the business itself will continue to generate enough money to repay its debts. And that's where artificial intelligence introduces an entirely different kind of risk.
turns.zh: 但更高的借贷成本只是问题的一部分，因为投资者还必须考虑另一个问题：这门生意本身还能不能持续赚到足够的钱来还债。而这正是人工智能带来一种全然不同类型的风险的地方。

turns.en: We spent a lot of time on the bid discussing the potential benefits of artificial intelligence. How it could improve productivity, accelerate scientific discoveries, and create entirely new businesses. The technological innovation doesn't benefit every company equally. Think about the internet.
turns.zh: 我们在 The Bid 上花了大量时间讨论人工智能可能带来的好处：它如何提升生产率、加速科学发现，以及创造出全新的生意。但技术创新并不会让每家公司平等受益。想想互联网吧。

turns.en: It created enormous opportunities for businesses that could adapt, but it also disrupted established industries and companies whose products and services became less valuable. AI could create a similar divide, and one of the industries where investors have already been asking difficult questions is software.
turns.zh: 互联网给那些能适应的企业创造了巨大机会，但它也颠覆了一些成熟行业，以及那些产品和服务变得不那么值钱的公司。AI 可能会造成类似的分化，而投资者已经开始追问一些棘手问题的行业之一，就是软件业。

turns.en: In our technology tour, Tony Kim explained that while AI has created enormous demand for the infrastructure needed to build and run these systems, it's also raised questions about the future of existing software businesses. At the top layer, the third main category, there's a few areas here, but that is really
turns.zh: 在我们的科技巡访中，Tony Kim 解释说，虽然 AI 为搭建和运行这些系统所需的基础设施创造了巨大需求，但它同时也让人们对现有软件生意的未来打上了问号。在最上面那一层，也就是第三个大类，这里有几个领域，但那其实

turns.en: what I would call the applications and services. And when you look at that layer, there's more questions being asked. You've seen the SASPocalypse concerns run all these various service industries also being disrupted. That's been a difficult area of the stack in the last three years.
turns.zh: 就是我所谓的应用与服务（applications and services）层。当你看这一层的时候，被问到的问题就更多了。你已经看到了 SaaS 末日（SaaS-pocalypse）那种担忧，还有各种各样的服务行业也在被颠覆。在过去三年里，这一直是整个技术栈（stack）中比较难做的一块。

turns.en: In fact, when you look at these three layers, there has been trillions of dollars of value that have shifted from that top layer down to the model and the computer. That concern comes down to a fairly straightforward question. If AI can perform tasks that previously required specialized software, what happens to the
turns.zh: 事实上，当你看这三层的时候，有数万亿美元的价值已经从最上面那层转移到了模型层和算力层。而那份担忧归结起来，是一个相当直白的问题：如果 AI 能够完成过去需要专门软件才能做的任务，那么那些

turns.en: companies selling that software? Of course, not every software business faces the same risk. Some provide services that are deeply embedded in their customer's operations. They may have access to proprietary data, longstanding relationships, and products that would be difficult or expensive to replace.
turns.zh: 卖这类软件的公司会怎么样？当然，不是每一家软件企业面临的风险都一样。有些公司提供的服务已经深度嵌入客户的运营之中。它们可能拥有专有数据（proprietary data）、长期建立的合作关系，以及难以替换或替换成本很高的产品。

turns.en: Users may offer more specialized services that could become easier to replicate using AI. That difference matters enormously when you're deciding whether to lend money to a business. Jose told me that credit investors are already distinguishing between these different types of companies.
turns.zh: 另一些公司提供的服务更专门化，但用 AI 反而可能更容易被复制出来。当你要决定是否把钱借给一家企业时，这个差别极其重要。Jose 告诉我，信用投资者已经在区分这几类不同的公司了。

turns.en: Six months later or eight months later, what we are seeing is that the market again has on the work, has understand how that risk plays out, and it's starting to differentiate those large software companies that have some real advantage in terms of being mission-critical
turns.zh: 六个月后、八个月后，我们看到的是，市场又一次做了功课、理解了这种风险会怎么演化，并开始区分出那些大型软件公司——它们在“不可或缺（mission-critical）”这一点上

turns.en: in terms of having a very large set of clients and distributions, in terms of having access or proprietary data that is very hard to move to a different platform. That's an important distinction. For an established software company with millions of customers and services that businesses
turns.zh: 有着真正的优势，在拥有极其庞大的客户群和分销渠道这一点上有着优势，在拥有很难迁移到别的平台的专有数据这一点上也有着优势。这是一个重要的区分。对一家拥有数百万客户、其服务是众多企业

turns.en: depend on every day, AI might actually create opportunities to improve its products and become more efficient. But a smaller company offering a more easily replaceable service could face a very different future. And this is where the conversation about AI becomes particularly relevant to corporate credit.
turns.zh: 每天都依赖的成熟软件公司来说，AI 反而可能创造出改进产品、提升效率的机会。但一家规模较小、提供的服务更容易被替代的公司，可能面对的是一个非常不一样的未来。而这正是关于 AI 的讨论与公司信用变得特别相关的地方。

turns.en: Because the risk isn't simply that a company's stock price might fall, it's that its underlying business could become less valuable. Its future revenues could weaken, and its ability to repay debt could come under pressure. That becomes especially concerning when a company has borrowed heavily.
turns.zh: 因为风险不只是公司股价可能下跌，而是它底层的生意可能变得不那么值钱。它未来的收入可能走弱，偿债能力可能承压。当一家公司借了很多债时，这一点就尤其令人担忧。

turns.en: Jose highlighted how some smaller software businesses were acquired, when interest rates were much lower, and valuations were considerably higher. The main risk that we're seeing in this part of our job here in credit markets is to look more at these smaller players, small software companies, a lot of them own privately, like
turns.zh: Jose 特别指出，一些规模较小的软件企业，是在利率低得多、估值高得多的时候被收购的。我们在信用市场这部分工作中看到的主要风险，是要更多地去关注这些较小的玩家、小型软件公司，其中很多是私人持有的，也就是

turns.en: no listed, and a lot of them were acquired at a period where interest rates were very low, but also leveraged very highly because the multiples of those businesses is very highly. Let's unpack why that's important. Imagine a software company that was purchased a few years ago for a high valuation.
turns.zh: 没有上市的，而且很多是在利率非常低的时期被收购的，同时杠杆也加得非常高，因为这些公司的估值倍数（multiples）非常高。我们来拆解一下为什么这一点很重要。想象一家软件公司，几年前以很高的估值被买了下来。

turns.en: The buyer financed part of that acquisition by borrowing money, expecting the company's revenues and value to continue growing. But now AI is changing the competitive landscape. Perhaps customers are finding alternative products. Perhaps the company's growth expectations are weakening, and perhaps investors no longer
turns.zh: 买家通过借钱为这笔收购提供了部分资金，指望公司的收入和价值能继续增长。但现在 AI 正在改变竞争格局。也许客户在寻找替代产品，也许公司的增长预期在走弱，也许投资者不再

turns.en: believe the business is worth what it was when the debt was first taken on. The company still owes that money, but if its value has fallen, borrowing again to repay its existing lenders could become much harder, and that combination of a changing business model and significant debt could create real problems.
turns.zh: 相信这门生意还值当初举债时的那个价。公司仍然欠着那笔钱，但如果它的价值已经下降，那么再借钱去偿还原有债权人就会变得困难得多。而商业模式的改变加上沉重的债务，这种组合可能会带来真正的麻烦。

turns.en: First of all, Jose described the challenge. That's where we are seeing a bit more pressure. These companies have less mission critical, they tend to be more regional or more sector-specific, and they are a bit less defensive. Now, that doesn't mean we're facing a widespread wave of defaults across the software industry.
turns.zh: Jose 描述了这一挑战的所在。这正是我们看到压力更大一些的地方。这些公司的业务不那么不可或缺，往往更偏区域性或者更偏某个细分行业，防御性也要弱一些。当然，这并不意味着我们即将面对整个软件行业的大规模违约潮（wave of defaults）。

turns.en: Jose was careful to distinguish the more vulnerable parts of the market from the broader universe of companies borrowing money. But it does demonstrate why investors need to look beyond the headline story of AI-driven growth. The same technology that could make one business more profitable might weaken another.
turns.zh: Jose 特意把市场中更脆弱的部分，与更广泛的举债企业群体区分开来。但这确实说明了，为什么投资者需要跳出“AI 驱动增长”这个头条故事去看问题。同一项技术，可能让一门生意更赚钱，也可能削弱另一门生意。

turns.en: And for a heavily indebted company, that disruption could have serious consequences. It's also a reminder that credit risk isn't static. A company that looked like a reliable bar or five years ago might face very different challenges today. Even if it hasn't fundamentally changed the way it operates.
turns.zh: 而对于一家债务沉重的公司来说，这种颠覆可能带来严重后果。这同时也是一个提醒：信用风险不是静态的。一家五年前看起来是个可靠借款人的公司，今天可能面临完全不同的挑战，即便它的经营方式并没有发生根本改变。

turns.en: Sometimes it's the world around the company that's changing. So what should investors take away from all of this? First, the extraordinary amount of money being invested in AI is creating opportunities across the economy. But that investment is also increasing demand for capital and physical resources, with
turns.zh: 有时候，是公司周围的世界在变。那么，投资者应该从这一切中得到什么结论？第一，投入 AI 的资金规模惊人，正在给整个经济创造机会。但这些投资也在增加对资本和实物资源的需求，并且

turns.en: potentially important consequences for interest rates and borrowing costs. Second, the impact of AI won't be evenly distributed. Some companies could become more productive and competitive. Others may find that their existing products and services are becoming less valuable.
turns.zh: 可能对利率和借贷成本产生重要影响。第二，AI 的影响不会是均匀分布的。一些公司可能变得更高产、更有竞争力；另一些公司则可能发现，自己现有的产品和服务正在变得不那么值钱。

turns.en: And third, those differences matter when it comes to corporate debt. When investors buy a company's bonds, they're not simply making a judgment about whether an industry will grow. They're also assessing whether that particular business can generate enough money to meet its financial obligations.
turns.zh: 第三，落到公司债务上，这些差别是至关重要的。当投资者买入一家公司的债券时，他们并不只是在判断一个行业会不会增长，他们同时也在评估这家具体的企业能不能赚到足够的钱来履行财务义务。

turns.en: And as the economy changes, understanding those differences could become increasingly important. Earlier this year, Jambavan made a point that I think captures the uncertainty surrounding this transition particularly well. I think the disruption and the disrupting, like the losers, will become clearer before we get clarity on the winners.
turns.zh: 而随着经济发生变化，理解这些差别可能变得越来越重要。今年早些时候，Jean Boivin 提出了一个观点，我认为它特别精准地捕捉到了这场转型周围的不确定性。我认为，那些被颠覆的东西、颠覆的过程本身，也就是输家，会比赢家更早变得清晰。

turns.en: In other words, we might recognize which businesses are being disrupted before we know which companies will ultimately emerge as the biggest beneficiaries of AI. And for credit investors, identifying those potential vulnerabilities is a particularly important part of the job.
turns.zh: 换句话说，我们可能先认出哪些生意正在被颠覆，然后才知道哪些公司最终会成为 AI 最大的受益者。而对信用投资者来说，识别出这些潜在的脆弱环节，是工作中特别重要的一部分。

turns.en: Because while stock investors may look for companies with the greatest potential to grow, bond investors also need to understand what could prevent a company from paying back its debt. That brings us back to the question we started with. Two companies might offer investors similar income on their bonds.
turns.zh: 因为股票投资者寻找的可能是增长潜力最大的公司，而债券投资者还需要理解，有什么因素可能让一家公司还不上债。这就把我们带回到最开始的那个问题：两家公司给投资者的债券收益可能差不多。

turns.en: But that doesn't mean they're equally likely to repay what they owe. Understanding their financial strength, their borrowing costs, and how their businesses might be affected by AI could help explain why the risks are different. And in an economy undergoing significant technological change, those differences may
turns.zh: 但这并不意味着它们还钱的概率也一样。理解它们的财务实力、借贷成本，以及它们的生意可能如何受到 AI 影响，有助于解释为什么两者的风险不同。而在一个正经历重大技术变革的经济体中，这些差异可能

turns.en: become increasingly important. For much of the past few years, the AI investment story has been dominated by the race, to develop new technology, and build the infrastructure to support it. But as AI moves deeper into the economy, the story is becoming more complicated.
turns.zh: 变得越来越重要。过去几年里的很长一段时间，AI 投资故事的主线都是那场竞赛：开发新技术，并建设支撑它的基础设施。但随着 AI 更深入地渗透进经济，这个故事正变得更复杂。

turns.en: It's no longer just about which companies are investing the most, or which technologies might transform our lives. It's also about which businesses can adapt, which might struggle, and how those changes affect their ability to borrow and repay money. And that is why corporate credit deserves a place in the conversation.
turns.zh: 它不再只关乎哪些公司投得最多，或者哪些技术可能改变我们的生活；它还关乎哪些企业能适应、哪些可能会挣扎，以及这些变化如何影响它们借钱和还钱的能力。而这正是公司信用理应在这场讨论中占有一席之地的原因。

turns.en: Because sometimes the most important investment risks aren't the ones making the headlines, they're the ones developing beneath the surface. As companies navigate changing technologies, higher borrowing costs, and an increasingly uncertain future. Thanks to Jose Aguilar, Jean Bovain, and Tony Kim for sharing their insights.
turns.zh: 因为有时候最重要的投资风险并不是那些上头条的，而是那些在水面之下悄然形成的风险——当企业穿行于不断变化的技术、更高的借贷成本和一个越来越不确定的未来之间时。感谢 Jose Aguilar、Jean Boivin 和 Tony Kim 分享他们的洞见。
